Phainon was used to this.

Every single step echoed as he moved throughout those halls, mechanical and practiced in his steps as he moved closer and closer to the person who had captivated him for so very long. Eyes focused ahead on the dim lighting as he listened to his own heavy steps - sighing a little over how he knew he would find that man with some random person nearby. 

A new one, every day, changing so that no one ever caught on to his acts and crimes - but Phainon never understood the need of it as he opened those bedroom chambers. 

Eyes dancing around the room to take note of how very dark it was, all before sighing over the dead body at the side of that luxurious bed, discarded, feasted on and tossed aside as if their life had never mattered.

And Phainon always felt jealous of them as he moved closer to bend down and feel for a pulse - sometimes ending their life so no one else would catch on, but usually just removing them from the vicinity with annoyance in his own veins. 

Today was no different as he moved to the side of his lord’s bedside, bending down to cock their head to the side - not caring for the blood that pooled at his own feet. How could he care about that as his eyes found those two puncture wounds on their neck - messy with blood that had been sucked out of them and devoured, but..

Phainon had always wanted that, to feel what they felt as that vampire asleep in his bed feasted on them - to feel those rosy lips and fangs sinking into his neck as his lord ate his fill, and yet..

It was never him.

“Phainon,” That voice made him pause, his gloved hand still cruelly wrapped around the latest victim’s neck before he craned his neck up a tiny bit - blinking through the sheer red and rather sparkly appearing curtains to find those feline-like eyes peering at him through them as well, “You’re.. Later than normal.”

Phainon had to smile over that - sweetly and softly as he fought down the jitteriness in his bones, barely even aware of the way he was assuredly going to snap the neck that was in his hands if he continued to look at that vampire lord. Unable to look away as his nerves twisted uncontrollably, sinking into him in such a delicious way as he repeated those words again and again.

Mydei had noticed he was here late. 

He had noticed his absence.. 

“Forgive me,” Phainon began as he dipped his eyes to the floor again - staring at the way blood was now ruining Mydei’s floor and he desperately wanted to clean it. That would have to wait until after Mydei spoke to him and gave him some attention, “I was a bit busy with other matters for you.”

Phainon could only pray that those few words were enough information - he wasn’t very fond of causing Mydei any worry as that man seemed to huff over that.

“You smell like blood,” Mydei grumbled out - and Phainon watched as golden eyes closed again in the darkness, all to be comforted with the sounds of blankets ruffling along with Mydei shifting his weight. Assuredly getting more comfortable to fall back into a slumber that was calling to him.

But Phainon had to drop his eyes at that, looking at that lifeless husk of a drained person who had most certainly been swooning into losing their life with how beautiful Mydei was easily.

Phainon smelling like blood was to be expected, after all, he spent most of his days slaughtering the commonfolk before they could ever possibly make it to Mydei’s home searching for answers. 

They knew a vampire lurked and ate off of them, what they didn’t understand was the man who seemed to stand between them and that fiend of the night. Always cutting them down as if they meant nothing, and for some reason, deigning that the vampire’s wellbeing was more important than theirs.

.. Which was a foolish thing for them to even wonder, considering how Phainon owed his entire life to this vampire who was now lounging around just a few feet before him. 

“My apologies, I’ll bathe next time I come up,” Phainon told Mydei softly, hands only tightening around that neck in his hands as he bit into his own lips. 

Mydei hated the smell of his blood - he had learned that much over the years as he stayed by that vampire, learning that he was so disgusting to the being that he could withstand keeping him around without letting instincts overtake him. Zero desire to taste Phainon, zero desire to put his lips on Phainon’s body, and that drove Phainon insane.

Every single time he was before that vampire, he wished that Mydei would drape himself over Phainon and bite into him mercilessly - and yet.. Time and time again, Mydei would roll over and ignore him, do his best to ignore the wounds from battle Phainon showed up and wait for him to leave.

The only saving grace was most likely the blood Mydei had already drank and let spill onto the floor below them both - a smell delicious to him enough to where he could ignore the unsavory scent of Phainon.

Phainon waited there for a moment, his eyes only staring at that lifeless body as he debated what more he could even say - staring downwards as he bit into his lip. Chapped and uncomfortable, if Mydei had a good look at him he would assuredly be less than impressed, and yet.. Mydei said nothing.

That was Phainon’s cue to leave, standing up silently as he did his best to pick up that body - eyes barely even registering the rather absurd hole in their stomach with a quiet scoff leaving his lips. Mydei only really got destructive like that when he was annoyed or angered and a piece of Phainon wished he knew how this meal had perturbed him.

Regardless, he made a movement to leave that room - hesitating to listen and see if that vampire would say anything more, all before sighing and leaving Mydei behind him once more. He would be back to wash the floor and get rid of the blood, but not before he bathed, of course. 

──────────────

“Mydeimos,” Phainon breathed out that name - a name that always settled onto his tongue in just the right way. A comfort to himself when he thought of who that name belonged to, yet now..

That man was hunched over in the woods, the soft creaks of wood and the breeze carrying the bustling plants to life. With only the moonlight beams breaking through the sparse trees to guide Phainon’s footsteps as he moved closer to the man whose hair burnt brighter than the sun.

More fiery and alive in the moonlight, even if he himself was straightening up over his name being said - clearly unexpectant of someone finding where he had dragged the corpse at his side to.

Mydei cocked his head to the side, and Phainon always felt his heart skip several beats when their eyes met like this - the briefest of moments that made Phainon’s mind stall and falter. It didn’t even matter that Mydei had blood on his chin, or the fact he looked like a doe caught by a hunter - he was always adorable to Phainon.

Their gazes meeting did even more wonders to Phainon’s body, feeling himself unable to stop the creeping smile on his lips as he visibly watched Mydei relax a little over realizing who it was. As if realizing it was Phainon allowed him to rest easily, instead sighing a little quietly. 

“.. Phainon?” Mydei asked after a few moments, his voice hushed, a lull in the space where crickets and the nightlife around them sang. His skin a beautiful gradient of red down his arms and to his finger tips that seemed to glow and shimmer in the moonlight just a tiny bit.

And Phainon could only smile over his name being spoken by that beautiful person, stepping forward to hear the ground mush beneath his boots, edging himself closer and closer to his vampiric lord who was still kneeling on the ground to feed.

.. That was always an annoying sight.

To see the man he loved so dearly on his hands and knees eating off the floor as if he were some type of monster or beast - it was a fate Mydei didn’t deserve, and one that made him angrily click his tongue over it. 

“If you were hungry, I could have handled it for you, my lord,” Phainon happily told him, though his tongue felt too big for his mouth - teeth too jagged and sharp for his own lies of happiness in his words. 

“I am capable of feeding myself,” Mydei huffed out as he shook his head, an action Phainon found himself easily adoring - watching the way those red tipped locks of hair fluttered about with that movement, “And I told you to stop calling me that, you are not my underling. You have free will to come and go as you please.”

With those words uttered, Mydei moved his gaze back to the person that was still lying on the floor - deceased, surely. But Phainon hummed over that, still moving closer as he moved to wring his hands together a little nervously. All before moving to fish something out from his pockets with a rather dramatic exhale leaving his own lips as he reached Mydei. 

“I’m aware of that, I merely desire to help and be as useful to you as possible,” Phainon murmured as he reached that man - not even hesitating before falling to his own knees beside Mydei, “Is that such a bad thing?”

“What are you doing? Go home.” Mydei growled at him, jerking his own head a little to glare harshly at Phainon. A vicious thing, if not for the way Phainon was clinging to the way Mydei had physically relaxed over seeing him.

Trust.

Mydei trusted him so painfully deeply, that was obvious - even if he was putting on this grumpy little face and snarling to try to make Phainon leave him alone.. It was cute, really! Feral little kitten who made messes with his meals!

Thus, Phainon could only crack a little smile as he palmed his handkerchief in his hands - moving a little to dab it against Mydei’s face and at that blood that was on his chin with a hum falling from his own chest. Delighting a little in the way Mydei was so blatantly shocked by that action - eyes wide as an owl’s as he stared at Phainon now. 

“You’re quite messy when you feed,” Phainon explained with a playful hum leaving his throat, unable to look away from that man for fear of missing the cute flickering changes in his personality, “It would be unbecoming of me not to wipe your face a little for you.”

Mydei didn’t shy away - even if he was staring incredulously at Phainon, blinking with such languidity that Phainon felt himself sweating beneath that gaze, and yet.. Mydei allowed him to wipe that blood from him.

He allowed Phainon that closeness, that moment together and gentleness. A blessing that Phainon was always thankful for, for so many differing reasons; even if he was wiping blood away, whatever Mydei needed.. He would happily accomplish it, if it was for him. 

“.. You are a human, Phainon. You should have issues with killing your own kind, and seeing me kill and eat off them. Not.. Want to clean their blood from me.”

Phainon found himself tutting a little over that, keenly watching Mydei’s eyes as they flittered away - dipping to the side to instead look at that decaying person on the floor. Someone who hadn’t enjoyed their fate, assuredly, yet.. Phainon was so painfully jealous of them to the point where he could feel his hands shaking.

Trembling, just the tiniest of bits when he considered Mydei’s lips on their neck, piercing into their skin and drinking the blood there - a thing Mydei had never done to him. A thing that Phainon was so desperate to feel, and yet.. He couldn’t bring himself to ask for more, not from Mydei.

Not when he had already done so much for Phainon already. 

Asking him to indulge Phainon as well..? He couldn’t.. He couldn’t do that, not yet, at least. Maybe one day. 

“Mm,” Phainon hummed as he still wiped away that blood, wasting time more than anything now so that he could keep that closeness to himself - basking in the way Mydei was allowing it,  “I am a human, that’s correct.”

Mydei still didn’t seem to look at him - but Phainon could hear it. The heavy inhale of breath Mydei made as if he was getting ready to say something, to cut in and argue against whatever Phainon had to say about it all.

The thought only made Phainon find himself smiling over it.

“But I’m so much more than that.. I’m a human that’s been blessed by a vampire lord. My strength is far greater than a normal man’s, and I find that makes me plenty useful for you.” Phainon hummed in an amused tone - unable to help himself as those golden flaked eyes moved back to him in the moonlight.

As dazzling as ever, beautiful enough to make Phainon’s breath catch in his throat as he stared at the way Mydei’s eyes seemed to even sparkle when the moon’s beams caught them just right. 

“If that’s wiping the blood off of you from people who are insignificant rats in comparison to you,” Phainon continued on before laughing a little, just a bit over the way Mydei seemed to be almost frowning over it now, “I’ve no qualms with it..”

“You’re.. A fool, really.” Mydei huffed out, shaking his head a little and Phainon had to resist the urge to move his free hand to Mydei’s cheek softly. Beg him to stay still for Phainon to clean him, yet.. He could only somberly smile at Mydei. 

“Am I? I think showing dedication to the vampire who saved my life, and decided to spare me is only natural,” Phainon told him with a toothy grin as he spoke those words, “You who feed off humans and slaughter them like it’s nothing.. Sparing someone like myself gentle touches while nursing me back to health..”

That was enough to make Mydei’s eyes dart away at that, his head turning more to focus on the person on the ground as if they were suddenly so much more interesting. And it wasn’t because he was embarrassed over those memories being remembered by Phainon, certainly.. Even if Phainon was very sure that man’s skin was turning to a flushed type of hue. So painfully lightly due to being a vampire with milk-white skin, but he.. He was stunning regardless with those tattoos that seemed to glow burned into his body as well. 

“You had a fever,  you were merely imagining such things.” Mydei supplied in a ruthlessly hollow voice - as if he was doing his best to distance himself from the memories.

An action or emotion that Phainon couldn’t quite agree with, only smiling more as he remembered the such gentle ways Mydei would caress his cheek while forcing him to drink and change his bandages. A level of softness that had never been spared for someone like Phainon, and memories that were so deeply cherished to him. 

“Mm, I’m sure,” Phainon chuckled a little as he shook his head languidly, “It does sound like me to imagine this vampire in front of me allowing me to be greedy with him.”

“.. You don’t know what you’re saying,” Mydei hissed out as he batted Phainon’s hand away, not even hesitating before standing up and walking past Phainon, “If you’re so eager to serve, you’ll get rid of that corpse, won’t you?”

And Phainon remained sitting there, looking a little after Mydei as he clenched that cloth between his hands over the newfound lack of Mydei. 

“Of course, beloved.” Phainon spoke those words with a small bow of his head, fully knowing Mydei wouldn’t hear that last word - but that was fine. It was for himself, anyway, licking his lips as he felt so painfully greedy today. Desperate, for more of Mydei as he moved his eyes to his bloody handkerchief - sighing a little.

He would have done anything to feel Mydei’s lips on his neck, and instead, that feeling was wasted yet again on someone that would never care about it nearly enough. Granted, they were.. Extremely deceased now, but it still didn’t calm the fire burning in his veins when he turned a little to blink at their lifeless body.

Just another one to be buried, just like the rest.. 

An average day, for the vampire’s dearest knight, he supposed.

──────────────

“You’re.. Early, Phainon,” Mydei said after a few minutes, making Phainon pause in that familiar doorway as he stared at that vampire - always eager to take in the sight of him active and wide awake like he was now, only..

Something felt a bit off, as if he was angry as Mydei sat there with his head cocked to the side - brows furrowed and knitted together as his jaw seemed as tight as possible.

And yet, Phainon could only smile just as he had always done; “It was an easy day today, are you hungry?”

A loaded question, he knew that the vampire was awake and sitting up in his bed leering at him due to his hunger awakening him - and Phainon only wished that he would say yes and pin Phainon to the bed and feast on him. Even if he died, that was fine, after all, his life was Mydeimos’s anyway.

Mydei took a moment over that, seemingly straightening himself out with a quiet exhale - one that shouldn’t have been audible if not for the way Phainon pricked his ears to hear every noise that man made. Every sound and huff that his body opted to give, all while waiting in that doorway to see what Mydei would opt to give to him today.

Whether it was only a few mere words, or a new order, Phainon was always more than just merely eager to accept them - anything, from Mydeimos.

“Yes,” Mydei mumbled after a few seconds of thinking, all before moving around in his bed and clearly moving to stand as Phainon merely waited - eyes keenly watching as that vampire stood up with a heavy yawn escaping him to show off those bright fangs he kept buried away there. Only the flickering light of the lantern in Mydei’s room to light both of their sight, but it was more than enough as Phainon blinked at the man.

Every single time Phainon was graced with the full sight of Mydei it caught him off guard a little - he wasn’t scrawny and pathetic like Phainon had expected and been told vampires were. Beings of the night who were quick on their feet and hid in the shadows, no. Mydei seemed to demand your attention by his mere existence as he moved fingers to comb through long locks of hair that always appeared much too soft.

Glittery, even, in the lighting when it hit the red hues his hair bled into nicely - all to match those golden eyes that gave the appearance of being able to see through any wall Phainon tried to set up between them. Not that he had ever tried, but metaphorically, Phainon was sure that Mydei could. 

His body was nothing to bat an eye at either, the opposite of someone that could cling to the shadows and hide - much larger and dangerous. Fingers that seemed to pull into such sharp claws to easily rip the soft underbelly of humans, all while his biceps looked as if working on his body was partly his passion. 

Whatever the case was, Phainon was always frozen to take in his beauty with how easily his shawls and fabrics hung over his body - chest on full display with heavy beautiful crimson markings sprawling across his milky flesh, all to show off the dip of his hips before his pants. 

Gorgeous, a stunning creature that seemed more like the type of person someone would spend days painting - not someone that was merely walking around in the seclusion of nighttime to veil him and hide his beauty from the world.

“Would you like for me to hunt you a meal, or..?” Phainon began as he tilted his head to the side innocently, watching the way those gold flaked eyes darted to him almost accusatorily - staring him down before flickering away quickly.

Focusing on anything but Phainon, and that always had him clenching and unclenching his fists - begging silently for Mydei to focus on him, and only him. For who else did Phainon even need in his life to acknowledge he existed but the man who had given him everything and more? 

“No,” Was Mydei’s resounding answer however in reply, instead leisurely moving over to Phainon - all before pausing a foot away from him, eyes dropping lower to Phainon’s neck so blatantly that he couldn’t help but swallow harshly. Feeling his choker tighten with the bob of his throat while those eyes studied him closely.

And that seemed to make Mydei look up again, making eye contact before leaning a bit closer - almost timid before Phainon found himself going completely still. Rigid, even, as he tried to wrap his mind around what was happening.

Mydei was sniffing him. 

His precious vampire was sniffing at him so obviously that Phainon could feel the way his heart was speeding up, adrenaline rushing through his entire body to make him more and more giddy as he tried to rein in control over himself. Phainon could barely hear it anymore over his raging heartbeat in his ears - unable to hear the soft sniffing sound of Mydei inspecting him.

All before it was over before Phainon could even blink twice - with Mydei stepping around him with a heavy sigh.

“Goodbye, Phainon,” Mydei told him, and that made Phainon spin on his feet a little to look at that man - taking in the sight of the person he adored so very much, the back of his head looking a bit skewed as if he were looking down.

Whatever the case, Phainon couldn’t withhold his excitement that was burning his skin and veins - turning him hotter and hotter as he thought about how blatant Mydei had just been in his interest towards Phainon for once. 

“I’ll see you later, Mydeimos!” Phainon chirped in reply, feeling as happy as could be - on cloud nine even as he grinned at that vampire who was now languidly leaving their happy little abode, a home that was just the two of them..

But that was all Phainon had ever wanted - as long as Mydei was by his side, he still had a reason within this world to feel joy. 

──────────────

Phainon had been here for so many days, checking in on Mydei’s room only to find no one there to greet him - no vampire lurking around, and he was beginning to have a sickening thought that Mydei wasn’t coming back. 

That the night Mydei had acted so strangely was Mydei saying goodbye to him, leaving him there alone in the world once more. And that.. That made Phainon’s grip on the doorway tighten - dented nails scraping at the paint and ripping it so easily with the age wearing the paint down as well. Every single time he checked on that room to find no one, the sinking feeling of dread only got worse. 

There were no signs of life inside the home besides Phainon, nothing had moved or changed besides what Phainon himself had done. Even as he left the home in his white and blue armor, ready to fight whatever came, there was never any signs of his beloved vampire.

Not even any signs that he had left in a struggle, or fought anywhere - no matter where Phainon checked and hunted around, he found nothing. Not the slightest trace of his vampire, if anything, it was too clean.

Too perfect.

As if Mydei himself was trying not to be caught, avoiding Phainon of all people. That thought was driving him utterly insane, and every single waking moment he spent wondering if he should go out and search for his beloved vampire. Even the nearby towns had become quiet - no longer sending search parties for Phainon to deal with, and that.. That was worrying.

No search parties meant no one was going missing nor dead bodies appearing with teeth marks in their flesh.

.. And that meant there was no Mydei to be spoken of - gone without a trace, and every single day Phainon spent staying at their home, waiting for his vampiric companion to return home was another day that Mydei may be slipping further away. 

That thought made him want to retch and lose his entire breakfast - only able to continue every single day as if nothing had changed, checking in on that room that hadn’t been moved at all before living like he still had that man waiting for him to come home in the dead of night.

Until it was too much.

Until that once beautiful bed that housed a sleepy vampire grew to have such a thin layer of white dust appearing - marring its beauty and making Phainon move into that room slowly. Listening to the floor creak as he moved to stand at the side of it, a place he had been so many times - yet now it was foreign.

Unrecognizable as he stared at that empty bed that lacked two vibrant eyes that appeared to glow in the dark staring at him.

And that was enough. 

Enough to force Phainon to leave - finally realizing that it wasn’t his home anymore, not while that vampire was missing without a word spoken to him. All to make Phainon replay that night in his head again and again, those words he had said hung so heavy in the air still - words that haunted Phainon now.

Good bye.

Why was it goodbye, something so deadset and unwilling to change..? Why not a ‘see you later’? Or a ‘talk to you soon’? ‘Good night’, even? 

Good bye. 

Those words were chosen on purpose, Phainon knew that much now - Mydei had purposefully abandoned him, left him behind without a single clue given, and expected Phainon to merely allow it to happen. As if he possibly could live with himself while not having a single clue or idea what had happened to the man he loved the most.

Thus, he had to keep walking and hunting for that man who had stolen his heart and given him something to look forward to every single day - a thing that had vanished along with Mydei, and now.. Every day was instead spent asking about vampires, laughing with people in taverns in hopes that they would trust him more - tell him about the worries of the townspeople and go on rants.

Werewolves? Those meant nothing to him, he didn’t even bat an eye when they brought up those and grumbled over how they had been killing their livestock. 

The slightest glimmer of hope when it came to vampires however, that was a different story. Phainon always listened keenly, placing his elbows on tables and leaning in over his beer to listen to what people had to say about the ‘vile’ creatures of the night. 

They were always eager to speak to a man who was wearing armor, after all, surely he would want to lend them a hand? And perhaps in another lifetime where he hadn’t already been strung up and robbed of his honor; he would have.

But in this lifetime, the only person that had ever given him a chance and heard him out was one of those beings. 

And now his life had become a game of chasing after a man with the most fiery of hair that seemed to be blazing on ahead - never looking back, no matter how much Phainon was praying for it. All until a normal day of scratching his nail against the oak wooden table lazily - his eyes dancing over bounty and wanted papers as he tried to see if any of them looked like Mydei.

They never did.

Though, on this day, a conversation made his ears perk a little - striving to listen in to the words and rumblings of two men talking. That.. That topic was mystifying to Phainon - the laughter of men discussing a vampire nearby, one who seemed more stand offish than most the others. Vampires were known to be vain, and enjoy their lives - living lavishly if possible, but this one seemed more keen on hiding.

A smart play, surely, much less people trying to kill them for being a creature of the night - and yet Phainon couldn’t help the way his heart was thudding against his ribcage even as he asked for directions to the town where this vampire was feeding off of. His own thunderous blood in his veins guiding every single step in the dead of night towards his destination since he had never feared the night.

How could he possibly fear it, when this was the time of day Mydei was truly active, and he himself had swapped his schedule to sleeping during the day for a better chance of finding that man. 

Every single day was spent in that small town for the next week, staying in their end and hunting for the rumored vampire at night - days on end to only add to the growing counter fraying at Phainon’s sanity.

All before, the fruits of his labor and searches for the rumored vampire..Paid off. 

He couldn’t even process the man that had his back turned to him - but with how large that vampire was, not frail and scrawny like most common vampires, there was no doubt about it. Blonde hair that bled into red at the ends, all while being so unaware of Phainon nearing him.. 

“Mydeimos,” Phainon spoke those words in a hushed whisper - barely even audible to his own ears as he moved his hand to tug at his shirt, feeling sweat beading against his skin and causing it to stick to him so easily. His eyes unable to look away as he looked at that vampire, the man he knew and adored - the man who he was wholly enamored with.

That was enough to make Mydei look back at him, those familiar golden eyes staring at him so keenly - studying him, all before going wide - too wide, too shocked, looking almost appearing horrified before Phainon could even process those emotions. All he could do was grin over the fact he had finally found him, his weeks of searching weren’t for naught - that man was here.

Mydeimos was alive. 

Mydei’s eyes stared into his own - and Phainon had never in his entire life been so happy to see that burning gaze burying its way into the depths of his soul. Peering at him so mercilessly, all before Mydei seemed to break eye contact - looking away with a flick of his head as if he had seen too much of Phainon on display.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon repeated that word, that single plea as he moved a step closer - unable to stop his own panting as he felt a small smile creeping onto his lips as he stared at that man. Doing everything he could to control himself, though, everything in him screamed to reach out.

To run to him, to grasp him, to hold him and never let go of him again - and perhaps he should have done just that.

Perhaps he wouldn’t have lost him again.

Those were the thoughts he had in his mind as he watched that man turn away from him - a scene that felt as if it were playing in slow motion as Mydei full on dashed the other direction. And Phainon.. Phainon simply chased just as he had been doing for months.

Of course he did. What else was he to do in that situation besides immediately call out the man’s name in a yell that hurt his throat. A panicked shriek as he moved through those trees and branches that felt like lashes against his face, unable to stop the burn of tears as he tried to find that man. Moving slowly to look around for Mydei, all before he had to come to terms with it.

Mydei was gone again, he had absolutely run from Phainon - why? 

Why?
